### Investment Memo: TJX — November 20, 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD (existing holders) / DO NOT INITIATE (new money) | Conviction: **Medium-High**
**Price Target**: $125 (−11% from current $140.30)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
TJX is the highest-quality operator in a structurally attractive channel — 30.3% ROIC rising four consecutive years, net cash ex-leases, 125% cash conversion, a forensic-clean P&L, and a widening share of a counter-cyclical off-price market. But every valuation lens converges on the same answer: at ~26.5x forward earnings (a 21% premium to the peer median) with a 3.1% FCF yield, the market has already capitalised a decade of flawless execution. The margin cycle has inflected (Q3 FY27 gross margin −11bp YoY, the first decline in the series; Q4 guided *below* prior outlook), and ~$331M of one-time tariff refunds embedded in the FY27 base will mechanically depress FY28 growth. Great business, wrong price — this is a name to buy on the ladder below, not at market.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector rated **ATTRACTIVE** — off-price has taken ~950bps of visit share from department stores since 2022 and wins at both ends of a K-shaped consumer (UMich sentiment 48.1, saving rate 3.8%). TJX is the preferred vehicle: +459bps operating margin above peer median, most diversified, lowest beta. Offset: the discount-rate channel is hostile — 10Y at 5.13%, 5Y real ~2.7%, Fed hiking — which caps multiple-led upside and drove the −27% June–September de-rating. USD +3.8% in nine weeks is an unhedged translation drag on the two strongest divisions (Canada, International).

- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **MEDIUM (leaning low)**. 100% of stores in high-rule-of-law jurisdictions; zero sanctions/FCPA exposure; clean Item 3. The live risks are trade policy (Section 301 actions on Bangladesh/Cambodia/China; China exclusion expiry Jan 9, 2027) and a credible, well-telegraphed consumer class action over TJX's retention of $331M in IEEPA tariff refunds — $112M of which went to bonuses, drawing Senate-level criticism. Legal cost is small; headline and AG-inquiry risk is not.

- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: **Fails every value test.** DCF and owner-earnings converge on intrinsic value of ~$85–120 (central ~$100–105); the reverse DCF requires ~14.5% FCF growth for a decade versus a 6.4% historical revenue CAGR. A de-rating to the peer-median 23.7x on unchanged EPS is ~$116 — a ~17–25% loss with zero fundamental deterioration. Buybacks at 28–32x earnings are value-dilutive — a genuine capital-allocation blemish on an otherwise excellent management record. Buy zone: below ~$105; aggressive below ~$85.

- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: Real but decelerating. Raised 7,500-store target (vs ~5,100 today) underwrites a 6–7% revenue runway; FY27E EPS ~$5.22 (+7%), FY28E ~$5.73 (+10%). But comps slowed from +5% to +4%, Q4 is guided to +2–3% (slowest plan in eight quarters), and Marmaxx (~60% of sales) is the laggard. Growth reverts to mid-single-digit comps as the base case, not the bear case.

- **Quantitative Signals**: Composite 66/100, but fragile. Quality (92/100: ROIC 30.3%, negative accruals four straight years, Piotroski 8/9) and Low-Vol (85/100: beta ~0.25–0.59, 21% vol) are the entire bull case; **Value scores 30/100 — the most expensive name in its comp set on every metric.** Note: the momentum and alpha claims in the raw quant feed were invalidated as stale-data artifacts — realised trailing-year risk-adjusted return is *negative* (alpha −9.2%), and the stock is −16% from its June high. Factor crowding (quality + low-vol is the market's most crowded pair) adds de-rating risk.

- **Financial Risk**: **LOW** — one of the strongest profiles in consumer retail. Reported $13.5B "debt" is misleading: funded debt is $2.87B against $6.23B cash = **net cash ex-leases**. 98.6x interest coverage, S&P "A", Altman Z ~6.4 on market cap, FCF $4.9B (+17%). A −30% revenue stress still leaves IG-comfortable leverage. The only vulnerabilities are valuation (3.1% FCF yield) and that 89% of FCF is committed to dividends + buybacks — a capital-return risk, never a solvency risk.

- **Non-Financial Risk**: **MODERATE**. Clean SEC/DOJ record and no securities litigation are real positives. Offsets: a non-independent Executive Chairman (former CEO, 20-year tenure) atop a long-tenured board; chronic store-level compliance dings (wage-and-hour, CPSC's then-record $13M penalty, hazardous waste); and a **one-way insider tape — ~$32M of sales clustered at $157–169 (within 5% of the all-time high) with zero open-market buys in 12 months**, including the CEO, Executive Chairman, and CFO. Programmatic, but the clustering is the strongest independent bear signal in the book.

- **ESG**: **AVERAGE / NEUTRAL**. Best-in-class Scope 1+2 progress (−44% since FY17) and mechanically sound governance (80% independent, one-share-one-vote, 92% say-on-pay). No thesis-relevant cash cost (~$5–15M/yr penalties). Structural caveat: the closeout sourcing model that creates the margin edge is the same feature that creates forced-labour traceability (UFLPA) and recall-compliance risk — no Scope 3 target, no published supplier list. No forced-selling or re-rating catalyst either way.

- **Alternative Data**: **Moderately bullish with one sharp caveat.** News tone maximally positive (15/0), holiday search ramp intact across all banners, and the +8% post-print gap is demand-endorsed. **But TJ Maxx search interest is flat over 12 weeks** — the Marmaxx problem is not visibly resolving — Ross is out-tracking TJX (+7.6% vs +2.0%), and the EPS surprise cushion has compressed to zero (Q3 landed exactly in-line). Data ends 11/8, pre-Black Friday: the decisive window is unobserved.

- **Short / Contrarian View**: **No forensic short exists** — Beneish −2.66, accruals negative four straight years, 125% cash conversion. The short is a *margin-cycle* short, and the evidence is specific: Q2 FY27's 33.4% gross margin contained 2.0pts of tariff refunds (~$0.21/sh, ~15% of that quarter's EPS); Q3 gross margin fell 11bp YoY (first decline); Q4 guided below prior outlook on fuel/freight; inventory days up 57.4 → 63.9 with inventory growing ~2x revenue. FY26's margin gains were explicitly credited to lower freight and shrink — both cyclical, both reversing.

---

**Bull Case**
- Structural share gainer in a counter-cyclical channel: off-price wins in good times and better in bad, and the current consumer (sentiment 48, 3.8% savings rate) is the ideal trade-down backdrop — Q3 comps +4% with International +8%.
- Elite, still-improving economics: 30.3% ROIC (4x WACC), gross margin +335bps since FY23, fortress balance sheet, $4.9B FCF funding a $3B buyback and a rising dividend.
- Visible growth runway: 7,500-store target, underpenetrated Europe/Australia/HomeGoods, and a favourable closeout supply environment from tariff-driven order cancellations.

**Bear Case**
- Valuation with no cushion: 26.5x forward / 28.7x TTM at a 21% peer premium; peer-median de-rating alone is −17% on TTM EPS, and a 5.13% 10Y with the Fed hiking removes multiple support.
- Margin inflection plus a mechanical FY28 air-pocket: gross margin rolled over in Q3, freight/fuel tailwinds have reversed, and the $331M tariff-refund benefit (~$0.19 of 9M EPS) rolls *out* of the FY28 base — EPS growth reverts to ~6–8% regardless of operations.
- Core engine stalling with insiders selling the top: Marmaxx comps decelerated to +2% (flat search interest says unfixed), Q4 comps guided +2–3%, and the entire senior team sold ~$32M near the highs with zero buys on the 17% drawdown.

**Key Risks**
1. **Multiple de-rating** in a bear-steepening curve — the dominant risk; ~79% of the stock's variance is idiosyncratic, and quality+low-vol crowding amplifies it.
2. **Tariff re-escalation** (Section 301/232) raising landed costs and thinning the closeout pipeline that *is* the moat.
3. **Tariff-refund consumer class action / state AG inquiry** — low financial cost, high headline velocity against a value-brand promise.
4. **Inventory risk**: days at 63.9 and rising into decelerating comps — watch H1 FY28 gross margin for markdown damage.
5. **USD strength** converting International/Canada outperformance into reported-EPS drag.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
**PASS at market; pre-authorise a laddered entry, 3.0% cap.** Buy 1.0% at $118–120 (peer-median de-rate complete), +1.0% at $105–108 (Value's buy zone converging with Macro's bear case), +1.0% at $88–92. For a high-beta book, TJX is a genuine beta reducer (beta ~0.30, SPY correlation 0.17) — but note it has been a *performance drag, not a hedge*, over the trailing year, so do not buy it for downside protection. If ROST or BURL is already held, cap the combined off-price sleeve at 3–4% and prefer TJX as the vehicle. Hard stop on a weekly close below $119. Thesis invalidation: any two of — Marmaxx comps ≤+2% by Q1 FY28; gross margin <30.5% for two consecutive quarters; inventory days >68; FY28 EPS guide <$5.40; a filed AG/class action on refund retention; or 10Y >5.75%. Decisive checkpoint: **Q4 FY27 print, Feb 24, 2027** — the first quarter where the refund roll-off and freight reversal both bite.

**Dissent & data flags**: Agents unanimously agree on business quality; the Value analyst's intrinsic estimate (~$100–105) is ~15% below the Strategist's ($110–140, centred $125) — the price target splits the difference. Stale-data artifacts in the quant feed (price, momentum, alpha) were identified and discarded. Gaps: S&P downgrade rationale unavailable; FY2026 10-K/DEF 14A full text not machine-retrievable; Black Friday demand data not yet observable.

## PORTFOLIO CONSTRUCTION RECOMMENDATION — THE TJX COMPANIES (TJX)

**Price: $140.30 (close 18-Nov-2026) | Mkt cap $157.8B | EV $165.1B**

### 0. Data Integrity Resolutions (must read before the table)

Three agents disagreed about the price. I resolved it from raw OHLCV: **the latest bar is 11/18/2026 at $140.30**, confirmed by the valuation engine (market cap $157.8B, 1.125B shares).

| Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Quant used $152.93 "close 2026-02-13" and re-based all multiples +9.0% | **Stale by nine months.** All Quant valuations must be discarded. At $140.30 the true multiples are *lower*, not higher. |
| Quant: +26.8% 12-1 momentum; Value: $156.66 last close | Both stales. My own regression: **alpha −9.19%, Sharpe −0.248, beta 0.305, R² 0.029.** The +5.84% alpha claim is inverted. |
| Quant dismissed the 26.83% max drawdown as "a stale/fixed value" | **Quant is wrong; the number is correct.** $167.29 (6/12/26) → $122.41 (9/16/26) = **−26.8%**, reproduced exactly from the daily series. |

**Net: the momentum tailwind the Quant underweighted does not exist.** TJX is −16.1% from its June high, −6.0% over six months, and has posted *negative* risk-adjusted return for a year while the business compounded EPS ~14%. That is a de-rating, not a momentum trade.

---

### 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding | My Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector** | BULLISH — sector ATRX, TJX preferred vehicle | Medium-High | +459bps OM premium to peer median; off-price share +950bps vs dept stores since 2022. Own data shows TJX is *slowest-growing* of Big Three. | **High** |
| **Value** | HOLD / DO NOT INITIATE; intrinsic ~$100–105 | High | 28.7x TTM, 19.3x EV/EBITDA, 3.1% FCF yield; reverse DCF requires 14.5% FCF CAGR vs 6.4% rev CAGR history. | **High** (DCF inputs aggressive — see §2) |
| **Short Analyst** | No fraud; **margin-cycle short only** | Medium-High | Beneish −2.66, accruals −3.9% (4 yrs negative) — clean. **But Q3 GM −11bp YoY (first decline); Q4 guide cut on fuel/freight; inventory days 57.4→63.9; ~$32M insider sales at $157–169, zero buys.** | **High** — most differentiated evidence |
| **Macro** | NEUTRAL — favourable business, hostile discount rate | Medium-High | 10Y **5.13%**, 30Y 5.47%, 5Y real ~2.7%, Fed hiking. Multiple-led upside capped. | **High** (verified: 2s10s +39bp, no inversion) |
| **Fin Risk** | **LOW** | High | Net **cash** ex-leases ($2.87B debt vs $6.23B cash); 98.6x interest cover; Altman 6.4 on mkt cap; F-Score 8/9. | **High** (corroborated by my ROIC data) |
| **Geo Legal** | MEDIUM (leaning low) | Medium | All 10 countries high-rule-of-law; no material Item 3 litigation. Tariff-refund consumer action = credible new front. | Medium |
| **Nonfin Risk** | MODERATE | Medium | Govemance ADEQUATE (non-indep. Exec Chair); **insider tape one-way**; $331M refund/$112M bonus controversy with Senate criticism. | Medium |
| **Growth** | BULLISH — 6–7% rev runway, 7,500-store target | Medium | FY27E rev $64.1B (+6.1%), EPS $5.22 (+7.0%). *Report truncated mid-table; no valuation discipline.* | Medium |
| **Alt Data** | BULLISH (moderate) | Medium | News tone +1.00, 0 negatives. **But TJ Maxx search flat over 12 weeks — Marmaxx not visibly fixed.** Series ends 11/8, pre-Black Friday. | Medium |
| **Quant** | BUY, composite 66/100 | **Low** | Quality 92, Low-Vol 85 — corroborated. **Value 30/100 — corroborated.** Momentum +26.8% and alpha +5.84% — **invalidated (stale data).** | **Low** (quality/vol legs only) |
| **ESG** | AVERAGE / NEUTRAL | Medium | ~$5–15M/yr run-rate penalties = <0.1% of revenue. Explicitly not thesis-relevant. | Low |

---

### 2. Consenssus Assessment: **SPLIT — but a clean, diagnosable split**

This is not noise; it is a textbook **"great business, wrong price"** split, and the two halves are internally unanimous:

**Consensus #1 (HIGH agreement): the business is elite.** Sector, Value, Growth, Fin Risk, Quant, Short — every agent independently reaches the same conclusion. 30.3% ROIC rising four consecutive years, net cash, 125% cash conversion, Beneish −2.66, wide moat from a 21,000-vendor buying network. **The Short Analyst could not build a forensic short and said so explicitly.** No agent disputes quality.

**Consensus #2 (HIGH agreement): the price already capitalises it.** Value (fails margin of safety), Quant (Value 30/100, worst of peer set), Macro (5.13% 10Y hostile to 28x), Short (margin inflection). *Four independent methodologies, same conclusion.*

**Contested — and where I must adjudicate:**

- **Is margin expansion structural or cyclical?** Sector/Value/Fin Risk say structural (+335bps GM). Short says the inflection is here. **Short wins on the near-term evidence, and the specific numbers are checkable:** Q2 FY27 GM of 33.4% contained 2.0pts of tarif refunnds (≈$0.21/sh, ~15% of that quarter's EPS); Q3 GM *fell* 11bp YoY; Q4 guided **below** prior outlook on fuel/freight. FY26's margin was explicitly credited to "lower freght and lower shrink" — both cyclical. **Adjudication: the +335bps is real but ~150–200bps of it is cyclically peak. FY28 margin is flat-to-down, not expanding. EPS growth reverts to ~6–8%.**

- **Is the refunnd a tailwind or a headwind?** No agent framed this correctly. It is **both**: a one-time $331M benefit *inside* the FY27 base that must roll out of the FY28 comp. That mechanically depresses FY28 growth regardless of operations. This is the single most under-appreciated item in the entire book.

- **Value's $100–105 intrinsic is too low.** A 8.5% WACC / 2.5% terminal DCF on a 30%-ROIC business with net cash understates value; my honest range is **$110–140**, centred ~$125. I weight Value's *direction* (premium exists) heavily and its *magnitude* only partially. Note the de-rate math is milder than Value implied: at peer-median 23.7x, downside is **$116 on TTM EPS (−17%)** but only **$136 on FY28E EPS (−3%)**.

---

### 3. Position Sizing RecoMmendation: **0% now; pre-authored ladder to a 3.0% cap**

**Kelly test: negative edge → size zero.** At $140.30 you pay ~112% of my $125 mid-cycle intrinsic. Expected 1-year return decomposes as:

| Component | Contribution |
|---|---|
| EPS growth (reverted, ex-refund) | +6% to +8% |
| Dividend | +1.3% |
| Multiple: hold at 26.5x FY27E | 0% |
| Multiple: de-rate to 23.7x peer median | −10% to −15% |
| **Expected return (probability-weighted)** | **−6% to +9%, centred ~+2%** |

A ~2% expected return against 26% annualised volatility and a −26.8% realised drawdown is **not investable at size**. Risk/reward is roughly symmetric ($167 prior high = +19%; $105–112 macro bear case = −20% to −25%), with the left tail better-anchored than the right.

**If the portfolio mandates consumer-defensive ballast:** cap at **0.5% tracker position** only, with the hard rules in §6.

**Ladder (pre-authorised, no discretion):**

| Tranche | Trigger | Size | Implied multiple | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **$118–120** | 1.0% | 22.6x FY27E | Peer-median de-rate complete; momentum fully flushed |
| 2 | **$105–108** | +1.0% | 20.0x FY27E, 4.6% FCF yield | Value's buy zone **and** Macro's bear case (−20/25%) converge here |
| 3 | **$88–92** | +1.0% | 17.3x FY27E, 5.5% FCF yield | "Back up the truck" — cyclically depressed multiple on structural moat |
| **Max** | — | **3.0%** | — | See §4 |

**Why 3.0% and not 3–5%:** top-decile quality argues for the high end; three offsets cap it — (i) 21% P/E premium to peer median, (ii) margin inflection + refund rolloff, (iii) factor crowding (quality+low-vol is the market's most crowded pair) and 0.58–0.64 correlation to off-price peers limits incremental diversification.

---

### 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

*Holdings were not supplied; framed conditionally.*

**Correlation matrix (252d, computed):**

| | TJX | SPY | ROST | BURL | HD | XLP | WMT | COST |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TJX** | 1.00 | **0.17** | **0.64** | **0.58** | 0.43 | 0.41 | 0.36 | 0.30 |

- **Beta 0.305, corr to SPY 0.17, R² 0.029** → TJX contributes almost no market exposure. It is a genuine **portfolio-beta reducer** and, on this axis alone, an attractive addition to a high-beta book. ~21% of its variance is systematic; ~79% is idiosyncratic.
- **Factor tilt:** adding TJX raises loading on **Quality + Low-Vol** — the most crowded factor pair in the market. You are *lowering* beta while *raising* crowding risk. Those are different risks and both must be sized.
- **Duplication flag:** if the book already holds ROST or BURL, correlation of 0.64/0.58 means TJX is substantially the **same off-price factor**. Cap the combined off-price sleeve at **3–4%**, and prefer TJX as the vehicle (highest margin, only one with above-median growth *and* margin expansion).
- **Sector:** Consumer Discretionary / Apparel Retail. If the book is already overweight consumer, this is a pass on sector grounds alone.
- **The uncomfortable datum:** alpha **−9.19%** over the trailing year. Despite beta 0.30, TJX has been a **performance drag, not a hedge**. Do not buy it for downside protection — the low beta did not deliver it.

---

### 5. Entry Strategy: **Do not buy at market. Ladder only.**

The stock gapped +8% on 11/18 (from $129.85) on an **in-line** EPS print — a relief rally, not a re-rating. Alt Data confirms the demand backdrop supports it but also that **TJ Maxx search interest is flat over 12 weeks** while Marshalls re-accelerates. Management calls Marmaxx "self-inflicted," implying a fixable execution issue; the alt data says it is **not yet fixing**. A one-week pre-Black Friday signal is not confirmation.

Combined with the fed at 3.75–4.00% and the 10Y at 5.13%, buying a 26.5x-forward compander **three days into a relief rally, at a 21% peer premium, in a bear-steepening curve** is the worst-executed version of a good long-term idea.

**Rule: no market orders. Limit orders only, per the §3 ladder. Re-run alt-data search series after Black Friday before tranche 1 is even considered.**

---

### 6. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss (any tracker/held position):** hard stop on a **weekly close below $119.00** (−15.2%), which is beneath the 9/16 52-week low of $122.41. A break of that low confirms the de-rating trend and invalidates the "quality defends the multiple" premise.

**Thesis invalidation — any TWO of these, exit regardless of price:**
1. **Marmaxx comps fail to exceed +2% by Q1 FY28** (consensus needs ~3%).
2. **Consolidated gross margin below 30.5% for two consecutive quarters** — i.e. the refund rolloff plus freght/shrink reversal is not offset by merchandise margin.
3. **Inventory days above 68** (currently 63.9; was 57.4 two years ago). Packaway into decelerating comps is how markdown risk is manufactured.
4. **FY28 EPS guidance below $5.40** (<5% growth).
5. **A state AG or filed consumer class action on tarif-refund retention** → upgrade to Govemance/Nonfin escalation (currently pre-suit investigation only).
6. **10Y UST above 5.75%** → the 20x scenario becomes base case; multiple compression dominates EPS growth.

**Trim triggers:**
- Trim one-third at **$167** (prior high) if reached on **multiple expansion rather than an EPS upgrade** — i.e. P/E above 30x FY28E without a matching estimate revision. That is re-rating, and it does not repeat.
- Trim one-third if **P/E exceeds 32x** on unchanged forward estimates.
- Trim if the off-price sleeve (TJX + ROST + BURL) exceeds 4% of the portfolio.

**Review cadence:** Q4 FY27 on **24-Feb-2027** (consensus EPS $1.47). This is the decisive print — it is the first quarter where the tarif-refund comp base and the fuel/freight reversal both bite, and management has already guided Q4 *below* prior outlook.

---

### 7. Final Portfolio Action: **PASS**

**Do not initiate at $140.30.** Pre-authorise the three-tranche ladder in §3 (max 3.0%). Existing holders: **HOLD, do not add** — selling a 30%-ROIC, net-cash, wide-moat compounder incurs tax friction and forfeits compounding, but there is no case for adding at a 21% peer premium into a margin inflection.

**The one-paragraph rational:**

TJX is the highest-quality operator in an attractive channel — 30.3% ROIC rising four years straight, net cash, 125% cash conversion, a forensic-clean P&L, and a beta of 0.30 that would genuinely diversify a high-beta book. None of that is in dispute; eleven

## SECTOR BRIEF — THE TJX COMPANIES (TJX)
### Off-Price Apparel & Home Fashion Retail | Consumer Cyclical
*Data as of Q3 FY2027 (quarter ended Oct 2026); financials on fiscal years ending late January*

---

### 1. Sector Overview

Off-price retail is a ~$150B+ US channel (apparel, home fashion, accessories) built on a single structural arbitrage: buying branded excess/closeout inventory at 20–60% below wholesale and selling it at 20–60% below full-price, with no long-term vendor contracts and no markdown risk. The channel is **taking durable share from department stores** — off-price captured **65.7% of combined off-price/department-store visit share in Q1 2026, up from 56.2% in Q1 2022 (+950bps in four years)** per Placer.ai. The US market is mature and consolidated around a Big Three (TJX, Ross, Burlington) that together generate ~$95B of revenue, with TJX alone at 64% of that pool. Growth has rotated from US store-count expansion toward **international (Canada, Europe, Australia) and HomeGoods**, while the sector's demand profile has become counter-cyclical: trade-down intensity rises when the consumer weakens.

---

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Structural trade-down in a K-shaped consumer economy.** Off-price is winning share at *both* ends of the income distribution — value-seeking low/middle-income households and affluent shoppers "treasure hunting." Off-price visit share vs. department stores has risen ~950bps since 2022, and the channel has outgrown total retail every year since 2022.
- **Favourable buy-in-the-market inventory.** Tariff-driven order cancellations, full-price retailer inventory gluts, and brand overstock are flooding the closeout market. This is the off-price model's ideal input environment: better brands, deeper discounts, and higher initial markups — visible in TJX's gross margin expanding **+335bps since FY2023 (27.6% → 31.0%)**.
- **Underpenetrated unit-growth runway plus capital returns.** TJX operates ~4,700–5,100 stores globally against a long-term target well above 6,000, with Europe, Australia and HomeGoods the least-penetrated banners. A **$3B buyback** and rising dividend supplement mid-single-digit comps.

---

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Tariffs are a shared, sector-wide cost headwind.** Both TJX and Ross have explicitly cited tariff-related cost pressure. Off-price is *partially* hedged (much of its goods are domestic excess inventory, not direct imports), but not immune — and the hedge weakens if brands cut production and the closeout pipeline thins.
- **Discretionary demand is decelerating.** Apparel is among the first categories to absorb consumer pressure; low-income stress (credit card minimums, delinquencies) is rising. TJX's own comps are slowing: **+4% in Q3 FY2027 vs. +5% a year ago**, with **Marmaxx — the largest division — the laggard**, offset by HomeGoods and international.
- **Intensifying competitive rivalry.** A "brewing share battle" among the Big Three, plus Amazon, Walmart, and fast-fashion disruptors (Shein/Temu) compressing the value gap. Add wage investment and store-growth-driven SG&A, and operating leverage is harder to sustain than the last three years imply.

---

### 4. Peer Comparison Table

*Fiscal years ending Jan/Feb 2026. BURL's gross margin is not comparable to TJX/ROST — Burlington classifies buying and occupancy costs in SG&A, inflating gross margin by ~13pts. **Operating margin is the valid cross-peer metric.***

| Company | Mkt Cap | Revenue | Rev growth FY26 | 4-yr Rev CAGR | Gross margin | **Operating margin** | Net margin | OM Δ (3yr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TJX** | $154.3B | $60.4B | **+7.1%** | **5.6%** | 31.0% | **11.9%** | 9.1% | **+216bps** |
| ROST | ~$49B | $22.8B | +7.7% | 4.7% | 28.0% | 11.9% | 9.4% | +125bps |
| BURL | ~$18B | $11.6B | **+8.8%** | 5.5% | 43.9%* | 7.3% | 5.3% | +290bps |
| DG (value retail) | — | $42.7B | +5.2% | 5.7% | 30.7% | 5.2% | n/a | **−363bps** |
| M (dept. store) | — | $22.6B | **−1.7%** | **−2.9%** | 36.6% | 4.6% | n/a | −209bps |
| **Peer median** | — | — | **+7.1%** | **5.5%** | 30.7% | **7.3%** | 7.2% | +125bps |

**Read-through:** TJX grows at the peer median but earns **+459bps of operating margin above the peer median** — the widest gap in the group — and is the only large-cap here combining above-median growth *with* margin expansion. The department-store and dollar-store columns show where the share is coming from: Macy's revenue has shrunk at a −2.9% CAGR with operating margin down 209bps, and Dollar General's operating margin has collapsed 363bps.

---

### 5. TJX's Competitive Position: **STRONG**

**Rationale:**
- **Scale is the moat.** At $60.4B revenue, TJX is 2.7x Ross and 5.2x Burlington — 64% of Big-Three revenue. That scale funds the largest opportunistic buying organisation in the channel (~21,000 vendors, no single vendor material), which is the actual barrier to entry. - **Best-in-class profitability.** 11.9% operating margin, matching Ross at 2.7x the revenue base, and 460bps above the peer median. Gross margin has expanded 335bps and operating margin 216bps since FY2023 — genuine structural improvement, not just cyclical.
- **Diversification reduces single-market risk.** Four divisions across three continents (Marmaxx, HomeGoods, TJX Canada, TJX International) versus Ross's near-pure US apparel exposure and Burlington's US-only footprint. International and HomeGoods are currently the growth engines offsetting Marmaxx softness.
- **Defensive characteristics.** Beta of 0.59 — the lowest in the peer set — reflecting the counter-cyclical demand profile.

**Caveats:** TJX is the *slowest-growing* of the three off-price players in FY2026 (+7.1% vs. BURL +8.8%, ROST +7.7%) — the law of large numbers. Marmaxx, its profit centre, is decelerating, and the company is not immune to tariffs or to a consumer that is weakening faster than the trade-down benefit can offset.

### 6. Sector Rating: **ATTRACTIVE**

Off-price is one of the few retail channels with a **structurally rising share curve and a counter-cyclical demand profile** — it wins in good times (value perception) and better in bad times (trade-down). The sector is consolidated, entry barriers are relationship- and scale-based rather than merely capital-based, and supplier power is unusually low because the channel is a *liquidity provider* to brands rather than a dependent customer. The offsetting risks are real but second-order: tariff cost pass-through, a thinning closeout pipeline if brands cut production, and a three-way share battle that will cap comp upside. Within this attractive sector, **TJX is the highest-quality operator and the preferred vehicle** — scale leader, margin leader, most diversified, lowest beta — though at $154B market cap it is a compounder, not a re-rating story.

## 2. Top 3 Geopolitical Risks

### Risk 1 — US tariff policy volatility and the IEEPA refund reversal (Probability: High / Impact: Medium)

The Supreme Court invalidated a large share of the IEEPA tariffs. TJX disclosed **$331M in aggregate tariff refunds** "for a portion of the IEEPA tariffs it previously paid" (Aug 19, 2026 press release, via Yahoo Finance/ProPublica), and accrued **$112M of incremental incentive compensation and discretionary bonuses** against that recovery (Calcbench; Forbes, Nov 16, 2026).

The 10-K's forward-looking statement list explicitly names "international trade and tariff policies" and "tariffs on imports from China and other countries" among principal risks. The refund is a one-time benefit, not a structural margin gain — Q3 FY27 results (Nov 18, 2026) were flattered by tariff refunds (net sales $16.0B, +6%; comps +4%; EPS $1.39; TJX International comps +8%, the strongest division).

**Why it matters:** the refund is reversible in economic substance. Other tariffs remain in force under different statutes (Section 301, Section 232, reciprocal baseline) — PwC notes the ruling invalidates *only* IEEPA tariffs. USTR has launched Section 301 investigations into Bangladesh, Cambodia, and China (Mar 2026) and extended 178 China Section 301 exclusions only through Jan 9, 2027 — a recurring cliff-edge. A re-imposition under alternative statutory authority would re-introduce cost pressure into FY2028.

### Risk 2 — Asia sourcing concentration vs. a fragile US–China truce (Probability: Medium-High / Impact: Medium)

TJX's off-price model is often described as a tariff *beneficiary* — it buys close to need and can pivot to cancelled orders and packaway — but ~100-country sourcing means it cannot fully escape duty pass-through. US apparel import shares have shifted hard: China fell from ~40% of US apparel imports in 2017 to ~26% in 2023, with Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and India taking share (Rhodium Group). Nearly 79% of US importers moved some volume out of China during 2025 (EAW Logistics).

The Nov 2026 Trump–Xi–Putin summit in Shenzhen exposed how thin the truce is: new US restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, Chinese rare-earth export-control suspensions extended only to Nov 9, and both leaders publicly invoking "protectionism" (Reuters, Nov 18, 2026). TJX is not a technology company, but a re-escalation that hits Vietnamese, Cambodian, or Bangladeshi rates would strike its sourcing base directly — and unlike full-price retailers, off-price buyers absorb cost shocks through *availability* and *margin mix*, which is harder to model.

### Risk 3 — North American trade architecture (Canada) and European demand/sanctions friction (Probability: Medium / Impact: Low-Medium)

**Canada (9.3% of revenue):** USMCA entered its annual review cycle on July 1, 2026 and the joint review concluded without resolution — trade policy toward Canada and Mexico is now a recurring annual negotiation through 2036 (Geolegalpolitics; ICPA). A 9.3% revenue segment in a single country with renewed tariff uncertainty is a discrete, identifiable exposure. TJX Canada's 589 stores and its Canadian dollar revenue also carry translation risk.

**Europe (~11% of revenue):** EU ministers continue to tighten Russia sanctions (113 new entities, Nov 16, 2026; new OFSI guidance for UK businesses, Nov 2026). TJX has no Russia operations, so direct sanctions exposure is effectively nil — but UK/EU sanctions compliance obligations attach to its UK and European entities, and the EU–China trade confrontation (anti-dumping duties, Chinese export restrictions on supply chains) plus a soft European consumer are the operative drags. The EU–US trade agreement took effect July 1, 2026, removing duties on a range of US goods — modestly helpful.

- Governance is mechanically sound (80% independent, split roles, 92% say-on-pay, one-share-one-vote) — a positive screen for most ESG-constrained mandates, i.e., **no forced-selling risk** from exclusion criteria.

**Why not positive:**
- **No ESG "alpha" catalyst.** There is no credible path to an ESG-driven re-rating: no Scope 3 target, no supplier list, no ESG metric in executive pay, and a board that has litigated against climate proposals. TJX will not enter the top quartile of retail ESG screens.
- **Asymmetric tail risk in supply chain.** The closeout/opportunistic buying model that generates TJX's merchandising edge (and its margin) is *structurally* the same feature that creates forced-labour traceability and recall-compliance risk. This is a genuine, if low-probability, model-level risk worth monitoring — it cannot be fully mitigated without degrading the sourcing model.

**What would change the call:** (i) a **Scope 3 target and supplier-list publication** (would move to Average-Positive); (ii) elevation of an **independent Chair** at the 2027 AGM (Governance to 7.5–8.0); (iii) conversely, any **UFLPA detention or second CPSC action** should be treated as a negative governance-quality signal, not merely a fine.

**Monitoring triggers for the investment memo:** UFLPA/CBP detention notices; CPSC recall filings naming TJ Maxx/Marshalls/HomeGoods; state AG hazardous-waste actions; EU CSDDD transposition timing; 2027 proxy treatment of shareholder proposals and the Chair role.

## 7. Confidence Level: **MEDIUM**

**Why not High:**
- Google Trends is the only true quantitative series and it **ends 11/8/2026 — 10 days stale, missing both the earnings window and Black Friday**. The single most decision-relevant period is unobserved.
- Each keyword is normalized to its own 100 max, so **cross-brand levels (TJX vs. Ross) are not comparable** — only momentum and seasonal shape are. Share conclusions are therefore directional only.
- A 5-year request returned an identical 12-month window, so **no clean YoY and no multi-year structural trend** can be computed. 12-month seasonal comparison is contaminated by non-aligned week positions.
- Web traffic and social sentiment are **web-search snippets, not API series** — no visit counts, no scored sentiment. Job postings and patents are unusable/no-signal.
- **No store-traffic, card-panel, or geospatial data** — the highest-value alt inputs for an off-price retailer are absent.

**Bottom line:** Alt data supports the post-print move and points to a solid holiday quarter, but it does **not** confirm that the Marmaxx deceleration has been fixed, and the estimate cushion is the thinnest in seven quarters. Treat this as a leading-indicator tailwind with a 2–6 week lag, not a definitive call — and re-run search data after Black Friday, when the Marmaxx question resolves.
